Anita — thanks for the minutes and the energy today. Short answer up front: 200M tokens/month is a reasonable pilot load for the configuration we discussed. Below is a concise note you can drop into procurement, plus two pricing scenarios (pay-as-you-go vs. committed pilot). I attached a one-page unit-econ spreadsheet.

Executive note for procurement (paste-ready):
- Pilot scope: 3 months, ~200M tokens/month mixed text + embedding workload (prefix caching assumed).
- Estimated unit economics (conservative): $1,800 per 1M tokens (pay-as-you-go); committed pilot pricing (3-month commit) target: $1,150 per 1M tokens.
- Expected monthly spend: pay-as-you-go ~ $360k/month; committed pilot ~ $230k/month (invoiced monthly against a PO or via a 3-month prepaid credit).
- Procurement gating: For PO-driven monthly invoices, minimum PO suggested = $20k/month (we can support smaller PO amounts but they may require additional billing setup). For a 3-month committed pilot we recommend a single PO for the three-month committed amount (or a signed SOW + monthly invoices).

Quick bullets on why committed band lowers cost: prefix cache reuse, reserved GPU slots (lower per-token kernel paths), and quantization profile selected for embeddings/gen mix.

Attachments: redwood_pricing_unit_econ_1Mtokens.xlsx (contains tiered examples and sensitivity to token mix).

Next steps I propose:
1) Procurement confirms whether they'd prefer monthly PO vs. single 3-month PO (cc Rajiv).
2) If procurement asks for SOW, I'll draft a tight SOW + invoice schedule for the committed option (Jordan to review).
3) Schedule a 30-min pricing + billing sync with Rajiv next week to close the PO path.

Happy to refine numbers if you can share the percent split embeddings vs. chat tokens (rough is fine).

—Karthik

Adding a couple practical points from an ops/implementation perspective so procurement has clarity:
- If Brightside wants monthly invoicing via PO: we need a standard PO form + billing contact and expected GL codes. Billing ops typically processes POs >= $20k/month without special handling; below that we can route to credit card or ACH depending on the org.
- If you choose the committed pilot (recommended for unit-econ protection): we will provide a short SOW that outlines deliverables, timeline, and a monthly invoice schedule. Legal review tends to be quicker if you provide a template SOW from your side — otherwise we can share ours.
- Timeline: once PO path is agreed, we can provision reserved capacity within 5 business days and target a pilot start within 10 business days.

For procurement: suggested language to accept into your PO request email: 
"Redwood Inference — 3-month pilot: committed capacity and billing per attached SOW; estimated monthly spend $230k (subject to token consumption). Redwood will invoice monthly against the PO. Contact: karthik_iyer@redwood.com for billing queries."

I'll draft the SOW skeleton this afternoon and circulate to Karthik/Monica.
